classifier_rationale: The customer cancelled within the free-cancellation window, received a cancellation code, and was promised a refund to the card that has not posted.

retrieved.text: Merchant credit wait period. If the merchant's credit or refund is dated less than 10 business days ago, set the expectation and schedule a follow-up. If it's older, or a statement closed without it, open a billing-error dispute.

Written notice link. After a billing-error intake by phone, send the cardholder a link the same day to submit or confirm the dispute electronically. The cardholder's submission is the written notice under REG-03. The call alone is not. POL-04 does not apply to UN, because notice of unauthorized use can be by phone (REG-12).

The 60-day window. The issuer must receive the notice within 60 days after it sent the first statement showing the error. If a statement wasn't sent, the clock runs from when it should have been. For a missing credit, it runs from the statement where the credit should have appeared.

note: Cardholder Yusra Haddad disputes a $460.00 Lakeview Suites charge dated 2026-09-08, posted on the 2026-09-18 statement. Cardholder cancelled directly with the hotel within its free-cancellation window about three weeks ago, received cancellation code LV-44910, and was told the refund would post within 3-5 business days. It has not appeared. Cardholder called the hotel front desk a couple of days ago and was put on hold. The expected credit date is not stated. Next action: open a billing-error dispute because the credit is overdue (POL-03), and send the written-notice link the same day (POL-04). Call is within the 60-day window (27 days after statement). Temporary credit not eligible (amount is $250 or more). Unknown: exact credit date and whether written notice was already sent.
